text:
deniz: Heads up — can we pause the planned runtime unpin for tomorrow 07:00 UTC? Canary for llama2q-13b-v2 is spiking p50 on long prompts.
aj: saw that. Do we have an initial hypothesis? KV-cache miss, batching, or kernel mismatch?
maya: quick check — kvcache hit rate dropped ~40% for requests >1024 tokens during the canary window. Batching tail latency also jumped. Not yet sure which change triggered it.
sasha: which runtime change was scheduled to unpin? I thought we were unpinning runtime 2.14.1 for the new kernel selector.
deniz: correct — plan was to remove the pin to enable kernel-selection improvements. Canary started after enabling the selector on the canary shard.
aj: ok, if selector causes regression for long sequences we should hold. Impact on hosted customers is non-trivial.
ops_lead: +1 to holding. Can we limit the roll-back surface? i.e., keep selector on for short-seq traffic and disable for long-seq routes.
maya: that's possible via routing policy by max_sequence_length. But rollout code doesn't support mixed kernel per-request yet without a small shim.
deniz: temporary option: revert the canary flag for kernel-selector on the canary nodes while we investigate.
sasha: prefer to pause the unpin globally until we confirm. Safer and simpler.
aj: agreed. What's the action plan? Who will revert? ETA?
maya: I can revert the canary flag now and run a quick canary for 30m. Steps:
1) flip canary flag off on canary pool
2) monitor kvcache and p50 for long prompts
3) if stable, hold unpin for next change window and do deeper analysis

maya: monitoring metrics now. Initial 10m looks better — kvcache hit rate back up to baseline, p50 normalized.
deniz: good. Let's document a formal hold and add compatibility notes to the release PR.
sasha: I'll update the release notes: mark runtime unpin "on hold" and add compatibility caveat: "kernel-selector may regress for long-sequence workloads; investigating KV-cache interaction".

sasha: PR snippet to add:

```text
- Runtime unpin scheduled for 2030127200: HOLD
  Reason: observed p50 latency regressions for long-sequence workloads with kernel-selector enabled on canary. Investigation in progress.
  Mitigation: revert kernel-selector on canary; hold global unpin until fix validated.
```

aj: also add a note for support: query for customers using >1024 token routes and offer to pin them if they see errors.

ops_lead: set the next review checkpoint for 2030134400 (24h) and keep change window locked unless we have a targeted fix.

deniz: I'll own deep-dive with runtime team. Suspect a cache-compat edge in the selector heuristics.
maya: sending log samples to the runtime channel and attaching sample requests.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy: none (pin hold active). No unpin operation in the next change window.

deniz: thanks everyone. We'll reconvene in the review checkpoint or earlier if we find root cause.

sasha: filing a short postmortem note in eng-releases/rt-unpin-2030123456-thread for record and release audit.

aj: thanks — and :thumbsup: for quick revert.
